_meta.batch: NP I – Community Health Nursing, Visual Aids Patch 2
_meta.note: Expansion beyond the Tier 1 box-flowcharts in patch 1. Adds Tier 2 (relationship/data visuals: Venn, timelines, trend chart) and Tier 3 (Picmonic-style spotlight-contrast mnemonics for hard-to-recall discrete facts). Every visual was fact-checked against the reviewed lesson it illustrates before shipping — no visual asserts a number or term the lesson text does not verify. Tier 3 uses one consistent grammar: a muted panel for the common/expected case, a colored 'spotlight' panel for the exam-key fact, and a lavender badge (star = the answer to memorize; ≠ = 'these two are different') as a repeating visual motif. Colors carry meaning (app brand palette, hardcoded hex so each SVG is self-contained). viewBox='0 0 380 H' for the 375px mobile-first constraint. Legal/definitional lessons with no sequential/spatial/magnitude structure remain intentionally undiagrammed.

visual_aids.title: PHC philosophy to UHC law — timeline
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 220" width="100%" role="img"><title>From PHC philosophy to UHC law</title><desc>Two milestones: the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration establishing Primary Health Care as a philosophy, and the 2019 Universal Health Care Act (RA 11223) making it Philippine law.</desc><text x="190" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="16" fill="#453A50">From PHC philosophy to UHC law</text><line x1="70" y1="116" x2="310" y2="116" stroke="#E8E0D8" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M300,110 L312,116 L300,122 Z" fill="#B8AFBF"/><circle cx="110" cy="116" r="13" fill="#5E93BE"/><circle cx="270" cy="116" r="13" fill="#8B72D8"/><text x="110" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="20" fill="#5E93BE">1978</text><text x="110" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="11" fill="#453A50">Alma-Ata</text><text x="110" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">PHC:</text><text x="110" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">a philosophy</text><text x="270" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="20" fill="#8B72D8">2019</text><text x="270" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="11" fill="#453A50">RA 11223</text><text x="270" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">UHC:</text><text x="270" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">the law</text><text x="190" y="204" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">1978 gave the philosophy; 2019 made it Philippine law.</text></svg>

visual_aids.title: Two immunization milestones
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 232" width="100%" role="img"><title>Two immunization milestones to know</title><desc>From birth to the first birthday: the Hepatitis B birth dose is given within 24 hours of birth, and a Fully Immunized Child has completed all primary doses before 12 months.</desc><text x="190" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="16" fill="#453A50">Two immunization milestones</text><line x1="52" y1="120" x2="328" y2="120" stroke="#E8E0D8" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="80" cy="120" r="11" fill="#E36B8D"/><text x="80" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="12" fill="#453A50">Birth</text><rect x="22" y="58" width="116" height="46" rx="10" fill="#FBE7ED"/><text x="80" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="12" fill="#C7517F">Hep B dose</text><text x="80" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#7A6E86">within 24 hours</text><circle cx="300" cy="120" r="11" fill="#6FA86B"/><text x="300" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="12" fill="#453A50">12 mo</text><rect x="212" y="58" width="146" height="46" rx="10" fill="#EEF5ED"/><text x="285" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="12" fill="#4C864A">Fully Immunized</text><text x="285" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#7A6E86">all primary doses before 1 yr</text><text x="190" y="186" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">The two dates the reviewed lesson pins down —</text><text x="190" y="202" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">not a full month-by-month schedule.</text></svg>

visual_aids.title: HIV testing self-consent: ages 15 to below 18
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 248" width="100%" role="img"><title>Who can consent to their own HIV test</title><desc>Under RA 11166, minors aged 15 to below 18 may consent to their own HIV test without parental permission; visual_aids.title: Cord clamping: the 1–3 minute window
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 246" width="100%" role="img"><title>When is the cord clamped in Unang Yakap</title><desc>In Unang Yakap step two, the cord is clamped 1 to 3 minutes after birth — delayed, not immediate.</desc><text x="190" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="16" fill="#453A50">When is the cord clamped?</text><circle cx="104" cy="134" r="66" fill="#fff" stroke="#E8E0D8" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M104,134 L104,68 A66,66 0 0 1 161.2,167 Z" fill="#6FA86B" fill-opacity="0.20" stroke="#6FA86B" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="104" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#B8AFBF">0</text><text x="180" y="138" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="12" fill="#6FA86B">1</text><text x="128" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="12" fill="#6FA86B">3</text><line x1="96" y1="126" x2="112" y2="142" stroke="#E36B8D" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round"/><line x1="112" y1="126" x2="96" y2="142" stroke="#E36B8D" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="286" cy="58" r="11" fill="#8B72D8"/><text x="286" y="62.5" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#fff">★</text><text x="258" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="9" letter-spacing="1" fill="#8B72D8">UNANG YAKAP · STEP 2</text><text x="258" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="44" fill="#6FA86B">1–3</text><text x="258" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="14" fill="#453A50">minutes</text><text x="190" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">Delayed 1–3 minutes — never immediate clamping.</text></svg>

visual_aids.title: MMR is per 100,000 — everything else is per 1,000
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 250" width="100%" role="img"><title>Which rate is per 100,000</title><desc>The routine vital rates — crude birth rate, crude death rate, and infant mortality rate — are all per 1,000. Maternal mortality ratio alone is per 100,000 live births.</desc><text x="190" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="15" fill="#453A50">Which rate is per 100,000?</text><rect x="22" y="46" width="150" height="150" rx="14" fill="#F5F0EB" stroke="#B8AFBF" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="97" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="12" fill="#7A6E86">CBR · CDR · IMR</text><text x="97" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="26" fill="#7A6E86">per 1,000</text><text x="97" y="154" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#B8AFBF">every routine rate</text><rect x="188" y="46" width="170" height="150" rx="14" fill="#FBE7ED" stroke="#E36B8D" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="342" cy="60" r="11" fill="#8B72D8"/><text x="342" y="64.5" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#fff">★</text><text x="265" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="14" fill="#C7517F">MMR — “Mega Mom”</text><text x="273" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="32" fill="#453A50">100,000</text><text x="273" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">per 100,000 live births</text><text x="273" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#B8AFBF">the odd one out</text><text x="190" y="226" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">Every routine rate is per 1,000 — MMR alone is per 100,000.</text></svg>

visual_aids.title: Total Fertility Rate below replacement
visual_aids.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 262" width="100%" role="img"><title>Total Fertility Rate below replacement level</title><desc>The Philippine total fertility rate fell from 2.7 in 2017 to 1.9 in 2022, dropping below the replacement level of about 2.1.</desc><text x="190" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="15" fill="#453A50">Fertility is below replacement</text><line x1="60" y1="60" x2="60" y2="196" stroke="#E8E0D8" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="60" y1="196" x2="340" y2="196" stroke="#E8E0D8" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="60" y1="150" x2="340" y2="150" stroke="#8B72D8" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="336" y="143" text-anchor="end" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-weight="700" font-size="10" fill="#8B72D8">replacement ≈ 2.1</text><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="270" y2="170" stroke="#6FA86B" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="120" cy="90" r="6" fill="#6FA86B"/><text x="120" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="14" fill="#453A50">2.7</text><text x="120" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">2017</text><circle cx="270" cy="170" r="7" fill="#E36B8D"/><text x="270" y="190" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Gabarito,sans-serif" font-weight="800" font-size="14" fill="#C7517F">1.9</text><text x="270" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">2022</text><text x="190" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Figtree,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#7A6E86">TFR fell 2.7 (2017) → 1.9 (2022), below the ~2.1 line.</text></svg>
